# RNBO codebox stateful smoke fixtures

These 13 original MIT-authored source forms target 12 exact RNBO codebox classes. They use RNBO `codebox~`, not GenExpr. Each `.rnbo` body equals the code embedded in its five-box stereo patch. Two separately declared state instances keep left/right histories independent; latch and sample/hold use the other input as control. No alias, GenExpr or patcher result transfers to these codebox classes.

The fresh-state epoch has **zero automatic preparation warm blocks**, four compared manual warm callbacks and sixteen compared timed callbacks. `reference_blocks` returns twenty full 512-word expectations and carries state continuously across them. The same 256-frame input repeats, with differing final/initial values and control states that make callback-boundary reinitialization observable. Zero-crossing inputs use nonzero signs, with a negative last sample and positive first sample to expose boundary crossings.

History uses its documented special value-read/assignment-write API, not an invented `.next(input)` method. Other classes use `@state` and `.next`. Slide rates are 2/4 and 4/2; DC gains are explicitly .5/.75 rather than default .9997. Their independent model histories use Float64 and a fixed `2e-6` absolute output error limit. Other expectations use exact dyadic/integer math and zero numerical tolerance. Accumulator increments are divided by 1024 in the authored source, with reset held at zero; no explicit reset mode is exercised. Delta clipping has fixed dyadic rise/fall bounds. Operation signed-zero differences are diagnostic.

Counter's reference policy is explicitly increment-before-output with initial zero, wrapping at 7/5. It observes tuple output 0 only; carry outputs are not qualified. The separately authored valid input-driven counter receives per-case input1 on both lanes. The original autonomous counter form remains separate: its input wires were rejected because a constant-only program declared no program inputs. Neither this routing failure nor another source-form failure implies that every API of an owner class fails.

Some boundary policies are declared because primary prose is less specific: downsample capture at ordinal zero then every 3/5 samples; zero crossings require strictly opposite nonzero signs, with initial zero producing no pulse; zero-count reports the completed 7/5-sample window total and holds it until the next report. Any discrepancy is retained under those policies rather than changing the reference after output. No arbitrary exact-zero crossing, reset, event, variable-vector or additional member behavior is inferred.

The independent reference and portable tests are `reference.py` and `tools/test_smoke_rnbo_codebox_stateful_reference.py`. Primary fingerprints and source/API syntax are in `catalog.json`. Generated RNBO C++ stays private. Actual resource preflight found no DataRefs or buffer-size requests among the accepted forms; the 4 KiB module arena is a structural ceiling, not measured use.

Ignored `build/research/rnbo-codebox-stateful-smoke-v1` preserves the initial exports and target build. `...-v2` preserves the original catalog/reference draft and separately authored input-driven counter. Actual parser/compiler failures remain in the merged module ledger. Hardware execution, actual memory and callback performance are separate steps; build wall time is not DSP performance.

The [XIAO hardware run](../../../../evidence/xiao-smoke-rnbo-codebox-stateful.json) completes 11 programs across 112,640 output values and twenty continuous callbacks each. Ten pass; `downsamp` differs from the declared initial capture-phase policy. No CPU-review flags or memory/allocation failures occur. The valid input-driven counter passes. The initial autonomous-counter graph is retained as an exporter port-validation rejection; the history source fails C++ compilation and is not executed.
